What we learned

01

Keep the prompt network blind

Giving it the scan made terrain tracking worse: error 1.31 against 1.14.

How it works
02

Remove the prompt network's average

Without that, every prompt leans toward one behavior, and sideways walking barely moves.

How it works
03

Seeing the ground can make a prompt stop

Backward walking stops on stairs and boxes, and adding such motion to the data did not change it.

Speed kept on relief
04

The choice is the weak link on flat ground

99.6% of chosen motions are carried out there, so the failures are the language model's choices.

Typed commands
05

A prompt alone can steer over stairs

P-BFM climbs 3.5% of stairs without its velocity command; SeeBFM's prompt alone climbs them.

Compared with P-BFM

With depth cameras

A student predicts the scan from two depth cameras. It crosses stairs nearly as often as with the scan, and falls more.

TERRAIN

Limitations

  • Walking backward and sideways slow or stop on stairs and boxes.
  • Blocks taller than about 25 cm are not climbed.
  • The camera student is weakest going down stairs.
  • Typed commands are done on stairs and boxes a little over half the time.
  • It follows few recorded stair climbs: 68 of 257.
  • Everything so far is in simulation; tests on a real Unitree G1 are in preparation.

Credits and citation

Motion from BONES-SEED by Bones Studio, AMASS, GRAIL, PARC, OmniRetarget, EgoHTR and LAFAN1; terrain tiles from PARC. The goal poses and motions to track are from LAFAN1 (Ubisoft La Forge, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, as retargeted to the G1 by BFM-Zero's authors) and GRAIL (NVIDIA, CC BY-NC 4.0). Built on BFM-Zero (CC BY-NC 4.0) and the Unitree G1 model. Simulated in Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab and MuJoCo, rendered in Blender. The comparison with P-BFM runs its authors' released policy in MJLab. Typed commands use the sentence encoder all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and the language model Qwen3-8B (both Apache-2.0).
